title: What are the two equal angles of this triangle?
description: A triangle has fifty degrees at the top and two equal angles at the base. The video takes fifty away from one hundred and eighty to get the sum of the two base angles, then halves it. A check adds all three angles.
teaching_notes: One idea: when two angles are equal, take the known angle away from one hundred and eighty and halve what is left. Watch for students who forget to halve and give one hundred and thirty for each angle.

source: Here is a triangle in which we know ∠B = ∠C and ∠A = 50°. Can you find ∠B and ∠C?
video_script.why: The child knows the three angles of a triangle make a straight angle and now meets a triangle where two of the angles are equal and not given.
video_script.substitution: Take the known angle away from one hundred and eighty degrees, then halve what is left because the two angles are equal.
video_script.anchor: a triangle with fifty degrees at the top and two equal angles at the base
video_script.payoff_line: The angles at bee and cee are sixty five degrees each

final_answer.spoken: the angles at bee and cee are sixty five degrees each

maths_rules: the three angles of a triangle add to 180°: 50° + ∠B + ∠C = 180°
video_script.design: The triangle stays in the anchor band with fifty degrees at the top and the two equal base angles marked with matching arcs. The working takes away, halves and checks.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a triangle with two equal angles.
<bookmark mark='top'/>The angle at the top corner, eigh, is fifty degrees.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>The angles at bee and cee are equal to each other.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you find how big each of those angles is?

beats.on_screen: the triangle holds still and Keeko sits at the edge of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko appears at the edge of the board

beats.on_screen: a triangle with a line XY through the top corner parallel to the base; the three angles at the top corner sit side by side along the line and make a straight angle

marks.line: the line XY appears through the top corner, parallel to the base
marks.three: the three angles at the top corner light up along the line

beats.colours: XY orange, base blue, angles green
narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A line through the top corner, parallel to the base, shows a fact about every triangle.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The three angles sit along that line and make a straight angle.

marks.given: the angle at A and the equal angles are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the angle at eigh is fifty degrees. The angles at bee and cee are equal.

marks.find: the question is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the angle at bee and the angle at cee.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the three angles add to 180°: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

marks.rule: the sum of the three angles equal to 180° is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the three angles of a triangle add to one hundred and eighty degrees.

marks.put: 50° is put in for the angle A

narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step two, put in the angle at eigh. Fifty plus the angle at bee plus the angle at cee is one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='take'/>One hundred and eighty take away fifty is one hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Together, the angles at bee and cee make one hundred and thirty.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: ∠B = ∠C, so each is half of 130°: 130° ÷ 2

marks.half: 130° is split into two equal parts and 130° ÷ 2 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step three, the two angles are equal. Each one is half of one hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='div'/>One hundred and thirty divided by two is sixty five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The angles at bee and cee are sixty five degrees each.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check, fifty plus sixty five plus sixty five is one hundred and eighty.
